title: Sectionwise pushout for completed constant coefficient maps
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E and F of Q_l, an algebra map i : E → F, a scheme W, and every pro-etale object U of W, the square of commutative rings formed by the constant E-to-F map, the two constant-to-completion maps, and the normalized completed coefficient map is a pushout. The maps are the coefficient maps of [def-pur-constant-scalar-tensor-data], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), together with the finite-free completed scalar comparison; basis-and-reduction construction of the ordinary coefficient tensor comparison.

proof.text: Choose the integral E-basis of F supplied by finite freeness. The compatible quotient bases identify each completed F coefficient section with the finite direct sum of completed E coefficient sections indexed by that basis. The multiplication map from the constant F coefficients and the E completion is therefore the universal balanced map. The residue normalization determines this map as completedCoefficientMap, and the universal property of tensor product gives the pushout. Compatibility with the pro-etale restriction maps follows from naturality of the coefficient maps; the empty site object gives zero section rings and the identity field extension gives the identity square.

proof_origin.note: Strictly smaller split from the objectwise ordinary coefficient comparison: only the sectionwise ring pushout remains to be proved.
